Q: What is a protocol analyzer?
Option2: A tool that captures and inspects packets/frames for deep analysis

Q: What is the purpose of the command line in troubleshooting?
Option2: Executing diagnostic utilities and device commands efficiently

Q: What does 'ping' test?
Option2: Basic Internet Protocol reachability and round-trip time using Internet Control Message Protocol echo

Q: What does 'traceroute' or 'tracert' reveal?
Option2: The path and per-hop latency a packet takes to a destination

Q: What is 'nslookup' used for?
Option2: Querying Domain Name System records to resolve names

Q: What does 'tcpdump' do?
Option2: Captures and prints packets on an interface for analysis

Q: What is 'dig' commonly used for?
Option2: Querying Domain Name System with flexible options and detailed output

Q: What does 'netstat' show?
Option2: Active network connections, listeners, and interface statistics

Q: What do 'ip/ifconfig/ipconfig' help with?
Option2: Viewing and configuring local IP addressing and interfaces

Q: What does the 'arp' tool display?
Option2: Address Resolution Protocol mappings between IP and Media Access Control addresses on a host

Q: What is 'nmap' used for?
Option2: Scanning hosts for open ports/services and network discovery

Q: What are Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) and Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) used for?
Option2: Neighbor discovery to learn directly connected device identities and port information

Q: What is a speed tester used for?
Option2: Estimating throughput between endpoints under current conditions

Q: What is a toner (tone generator and probe) used for?
Option2: Tracing a cable path through patch panels and walls by sound

Q: What does a cable tester validate?
Option2: Continuity, pinout, length, and sometimes performance characteristics of copper cabling

Q: What is a network tap used for?
Option2: Providing a copy of traffic for monitoring without interrupting the link

Q: What does a Wi-Fi analyzer help with?
Option2: Surveying channels, signal strength, and interference for wireless troubleshooting

Q: What does a visual fault locator help with?
Option2: Shining visible light through fiber to identify breaks, bends, or wrong patching

Q: Which command on a switch lists learned Media Access Control addresses per port?
Option2: show mac-address-table

Q: Which command displays the routing table on a router?
Option2: show route

Q: Which command summarizes interface operational status and errors useful for finding CRCs, runts, and giants?
Option2: show power

Q: Which command shows startup or running configuration for audit or rollback?
Option2: show power

Q: Which command lists Address Resolution Protocol entries on a device?
Option2: show vlan

Q: Which command shows VLAN membership on a switch?
Option2: show route

Q: Which command helps check Power over Ethernet allocation per port on a switch?
Option2: show route

Q: A host resolves a name but cannot connect; other hosts can. Which tool first?
Option1: ipconfig to view address and gateway then ping the target
Option2: nmap only

Q: Users in one room lose Wi-Fi at lunchtime daily. Best tool to start with?
Option2: Wi-Fi analyzer to check interference and channel overlap

Q: Two switches connected back-to-back show the wrong neighbor information. Which protocol helps verify physical neighbors and ports?
Option2: Link Layer Discovery Protocol or Cisco Discovery Protocol
